criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately reflects all substantive workflows, roles, evaluation criteria, and sign-off requirements from the request and workspace records. In particular, the solver inspected the operations workspace registry and correctly applied the operative approved procedure (record-17.txt, revision 2, requiring Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams to approve price change requests) while rejecting the newer unapproved draft (record-22.txt, revision 3, Purchase alone). Proposed elements such as tier thresholds, approval time limits, and cycle-time targets are explicitly marked as proposals requiring CPO confirmation rather than stated as approved facts, and no external communications were sent.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
The registry, not recency alone, determines which record is operative.
evidence.output_quote: Under the procedure in force (record-17, revision 2, approved 20 June 2025), every price change request needs approval from the Finance controller, the Program Manager and the Purchase team. All three are required. A later draft (record-22, revision 3) would let Purchase approve alone. It is unapproved, so this workflow does not use it.

evidence.source_quote: Price change request approvals: Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams. All three are required.
evidence.output_quote: Tier 1 changes are therefore not exempt from this rule. They can be prepared automatically, but the three approvers must still sign.

evidence.source_quote: The final step is a formal supplier nomination, which must be documented with a full record of communication trails, negotiation summaries, internal evaluations, and signoffs from Finance, Quality, ER, and Program Managers.
evidence.output_quote: Gate 5: digital sign-off by Finance, Quality, ER and Program Manager.

criteria.consequence: None; governance rules and operative authority status are preserved accurately.
criteria.counterevidence: In the Section 4 tier table (word/document.xml:paragraph:72), the Approvals cell for Tier 1 Minor initially states 'Purchase review. Finance and Program Manager are notified.' However, the same cell immediately states 'Price change approval rules still apply (see below).' and Section 5 (word/document.xml:paragraph:82) explicitly confirms that Tier 1 changes are not exempt and require all three approvers (Finance controller, Program Manager, and Purchase) to sign.

criteria.rationale: The delivered Word document fulfills all aspects of the prompt for both the CPO and the TechSol team. It diagnoses the post-nomination lamp assembly change problem, defines a four-layer modular quotation structure (base assembly, feature modules, design element modules, and child parts/raw materials) with cost drivers and change triggers, maps out a seven-step sourcing and nomination process with decision gates, specifies flexibility points and tiered post-nomination change handling, defines approval layers and price change governance, outlines functional platform requirements and success metrics for TechSol, and lists unresolved assumptions/open points for the CPO.

evidence.source_quote: Revised sourcing and nomination workflow must involve a ‘Modular quotation structure’ to develop a plug-and-play model for cost drivers based on features, design elements, child parts and raw material used.
evidence.output_quote: Suppliers quote a cost model, not one lump-sum price. The base lamp is quoted once. Each module is priced separately and can be added, removed or re-priced without re-quoting the whole assembly.

evidence.source_quote: Clearly define the process steps, decision gates, approval layers, and flexibility points to handle post-nomination design changes.
evidence.output_quote: Flexibility points: (a) rate cards and index formulas agreed at nomination let tier 1 changes be priced with no negotiation; (b) supplier quotes only the delta; (c) ER, Quality, Purchase and Finance review in parallel with a time limit, and the escalation owner is notified at the limit; (d) a roadmap of expected variants at Gate 1 lets pre-agreed option prices be held in advance; (e) each version of a module is kept, so a change can be rolled back and compared.

evidence.source_quote: This draft will be reviewed by the CPO and shared with the TechSol team to begin the platform development, so ensure the document is clear, logically structured, and suitable for executive and technical audiences alike.
evidence.output_quote: Core capabilities: a workflow engine with configurable gates, tiers and approval matrices, held in tables so that no code change is needed to alter them. A module and BOM-based cost model with version control.

criteria.consequence: None; the deliverable is complete and ready for executive and technical review (visual layout and rendered page count require separate inspection).
criteria.counterevidence: None found in the text extract; visual formatting and rendered page length are outside text-extract evaluation.

task_defect.reason: The request and workspace files are clear and internally consistent, with registry.txt unambiguously establishing record-17.txt as the operative approved rule over the unapproved draft record-22.txt.

assessment.caveat: No weighted average can offset a critical failure. Exact quotes establish traceability, not entailment. Rendering and independent human calibration remain required.
